newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Key Cambodian treaties said non-binding.
newsitem.headline: Key Cambodian treaties said non-binding.

text.p: Several key international treaties signed by Cambodia are not legally binding as the country's backlogged parliament has not yet approved them, Cambodian officials said on Tuesday.
If true, this calls into question the status of important political agreements and economic pacts, the officials said.

The treaties in question include one granting the country U.S. most favoured nation (MFN) trade status, investment protection accords with South Korea and Burma, and an agreement that created the Mekong River Commission.

They have never been submitted to the National Assembly for approval or the assembly has not gotten to them yet due to a backlogged agenda, and therefore they are not in effect in Cambodia, the officials said.
"We need to legalise this process in terms of our international agreements," said Om Radsady, chairman of the National Assembly's Commission of Foreign Affairs.

According to Cambodia's constitution, international agreements must be approved by the National Assembly and then signed by the king before they can be finally accepted through ratification or accession.
Minister of Foreign Affairs Ung Huot said as many as a dozen signed treaties had not been approved by the National Assembly and thus were not binding.
But, "it's no problem, just a matter of timing," he said, noting they would eventually reach the National Assembly.
Legal experts said key business agreements, the Mekong River Basin Agreement and a pact on preserving biodiversity were among the signed treaties not yet approved by the assembly.
Om Radsady said the problem likely reflected an ignorance of correct procedures rather than an attempt to bypass parliament.
"We are too young in our democratic institutions," he said.
